summary: ProjectService and ProjectController implement the platform isolation primitive cleanly: requireOwned uniformly collapses foreign / soft-deleted-without-flag / missing / malformed-ObjectId to AppException.notFound; both 409 paths use the two-arg AppException.conflict("project_name_taken", ...) so code propagates; restore enforces the Decision 14 deletedAt-FIRST guard and the unit + IT pair both prove no project_renamed/project_restored event leaks for an active project. PATCH-normalization handles the three blank/null cases per spec, mass-assignment defense holds (DTO @JsonIgnoreProperties + ProjectResponse omits ownerId), and AC-T7 zero-touch is honored — git diff shows only the five new files. Cross-file consistency (AppException factories, EventService.logEvent signature, ProjectRepository derived finders, ProfileController helper parity) verified.

findings.issue: getProjects_returnsOnlyOwnActiveSortedDesc relies on Thread.sleep(10) between two saveActive() calls to disambiguate createdAt-desc ordering. Instant resolution is sub-millisecond on most hardware, but a 10ms sleep is empirical — under load (CI runner contention, container clock skew) the two timestamps could still tie and the test would flap on `$[0].name == "B"`.
findings.fix: Either (a) seed both projects with explicit, distinct createdAt values via a saveActive overload that accepts an Instant (no reliance on wall-clock between calls), or (b) tighten to >=50ms if the helper-overload route is too invasive. Optional — Wave 1 review accepted similar real-clock dependence and the spec explicitly flags this as a tolerated brittleness.

findings.issue: applyDescription/applyTimezone/blankToNull are fine but the three helpers encode subtly different blank semantics (description: blank → null, timezone: blank → no-op, blankToNull: blank → null). Comments above the controller `normalize` describe this; service-side helpers are silent. Future readers tracing the PATCH flow will need to bounce between the controller comment block and the service helpers to reconstruct the intent.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment above each helper noting the spec mapping (e.g. `// AC-22b: PATCH description blank → clear (null in DB)`, `// AC-22c: PATCH timezone blank → no-op`). Non-blocking polish.

non_findings: Anti-enumeration: requireOwned wires all four code paths (foreign / soft-deleted-without-flag / missing / malformed-ObjectId via .onErrorMap(IllegalArgumentException.class, ...)) to identical AppException.notFound. ProjectServiceTest covers all five cases (happy + 4 negative) and ProjectControllerIT covers PATCH/DELETE/restore × foreign/malformed parity.

Decision 14 deletedAt-FIRST guard: restore() checks `project.getDeletedAt() == null` BEFORE quota / name-collision / save. Both restore_onActiveProject_throws404AndDoesNotEmitRenameOrRestore (unit) and restoreProject_onActiveProject_returns404AndDoesNotEmitRenameOrRestoreEvent (IT) assert that NEITHER project_renamed NOR project_restored fires for the projectId.

AC-5 / AC-12b 409 code propagation: both create() (line 80-81) and update() (line 111-112) use the two-argument AppException.conflict(CODE_PROJECT_NAME_TAKEN, MESSAGE_NAME_TAKEN). The legacy single-arg conflict(String) is not invoked anywhere in ProjectService.

Mass-assignment (R2): controller never reads ownerId from request body — ownerId is sourced from currentUserId() / SecurityContext on every mutation. CreateProjectRequest + UpdateProjectRequest carry @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) from Task 1. ProjectResponse omits ownerId. IT postProject_hostileBodyWithOwnerId_savesAuthenticatedOwnerIdAndResponseHasNoOwnerIdField verifies both halves (DB record's ownerId == authenticated user; response body has no ownerId field; OTHER_USER_ID has 0 documents).

AC-T7 zero-touch: `git diff 8cd8ce6~1..8cd8ce6 --name-only` returns exactly the five new files; SecurityConfig.java, auth.global.ts, EventService.java, JobRunrMongoConfig.java, AbstractIntegrationTest are untouched.

AC-T11: all Mongo access goes through ReactiveMongoRepository derived finders (findById, findByOwnerIdAndDeletedAtIsNullOrderByCreatedAtDesc, findByOwnerIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc, countByOwnerIdAndDeletedAtIsNull, findByOwnerIdAndNameAndDeletedAtIsNull, findByOwnerIdAndNameAndIdNotAndDeletedAtIsNull). No Criteria construction, no string concatenation.

PATCH semantics in ProjectController.normalize: null name → no change (passed through as null); blank name → coerced to null → no change; blank description → preserved as "" → service maps to null; blank timezone → coerced to null → no change. Matches tech-spec lines 236-239 and AC-22b/22c. IT patchProject_blankDescription_setsDbDescriptionToNull and patchProject_blankTimezone_doesNotOverwriteExistingTimezone exercise both branches with mutable buildPatchBody (Map.of would NPE on "" values — handled correctly).

Slice-test connection-factory mocks: empirical result — ZERO mocks needed. ProjectControllerSliceTest mirrors AuthControllerSliceTest pattern (only @MockitoBean on the service under test) and the @WebFluxTest auto-config alone is sufficient. patterns.md:38 mentions three connection-factory mocks for full @SpringBootTest contexts; that requirement does not apply to @WebFluxTest slices in this codebase. The test's own comment block documents this explicitly.

currentUserId / extractIp / capUserAgent are byte-for-byte copies of ProfileController's helpers (USER_AGENT_MAX = 500, X-Forwarded-For comma split, .switchIfEmpty(Mono.error(AppException.unauthorized("Not authenticated")))). Duplication accepted per task spec; the controller's comment notes deferral of a shared util.

Audit-event metadata shapes match the tech-spec table (lines 264-269): project_created {projectId, name}; project_updated {projectId} ONLY; project_renamed {projectId, previousName, name}; project_soft_deleted {projectId, name}; project_restored {projectId, name [, renamedDueToConflict: true]}. The conditional metadata key for restore-with-rename uses HashMap (not Map.of) so the optional flag can be added cleanly.

Event emission via .doOnSuccess: events fire only after a successful save; on AppException paths (quota exceeded, name conflict, deletedAt guard) the chain is in error state and doOnSuccess is skipped — verified by Mockito verify(eventService, never()).logEvent(...) in create_atQuotaLimit, create_duplicateActiveName, softDelete_alreadySoftDeleted, restore_onActiveProject, restore_atQuotaLimit.

GlobalErrorHandler integration: AppException.notFound(...) → 404 with {message, code:null}; AppException.conflict(code, message) → 409 with {message, code: "project_name_taken"}; AppException.unprocessableEntity(code, message) → 422 with {message, code: "project_limit_reached"}; @Valid violations → 400 with {message: "field: msg, ...", code: null}. errorBodies_alwaysHaveMessageAndCode IT exercises 400 + 404 + 409 to lock the AC-T1 contract. Spring's jsonPath().doesNotExist() accepts both "path missing" and "path resolves to null" — confirmed against existing AuthControllerIT.verifyEmail_invalidToken_400NotServerError pattern.

EventService.logEvent signature usage matches: (String userId, String eventType, String ip, String userAgent, Map<String, Object> metadata). Five call sites all pass the same shape; Map.of is null-safe for the four fixed-shape events, restore-with-rename uses HashMap to allow the optional flag.

Reactive composition: no .block() in production code; all flows are Mono/Flux; .flatMap is used for value-producing transitions, .doOnSuccess for side effects (event logging), .switchIfEmpty for empty-Mono → save defer, .onErrorMap for IllegalArgumentException → 404. Matches ProfileService idioms. No Schedulers.boundedElastic — correctly avoided per task spec note (no CPU-bound work like BCrypt here).

Test counts: 20 ProjectServiceTest (matches TDD anchor unit list exactly), 1 ProjectControllerSliceTest (response-shape lock), 38 ProjectControllerIT — sums to the test plan in tech-spec Testing Strategy and the task TDD Anchor.
